fact_text: Current account deposits pay the depositor nothing, so the spread a bank earns on them is much wider than on savings deposits that pay interest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Shifting deposits from interest-paying savings into non-interest current accounts lifts a bank's net interest income on the same lending book, so the current account share is a key variable to check when analysing banks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL's current account share of deposits rose from about 40% in 2019-2020 to about 50%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: During the 2024 tax on banks, UBL cut its high-cost savings and corporate deposits and shifted its focus to low-cost current accounts to manage the tax impact.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A deposit franchise built on wide branch and ATM networks and strong brand trust brings customers to the bank, which makes growing current accounts easier than when a bank must chase depositors with offers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL uses zero-cost accounts, debit cards and digital onboarding to attract current account deposits, which the analyst views as valuable for long-term earnings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario assumes UBL's local deposits reach about PKR 5.5 trillion, and with roughly 50% in current accounts that gives about PKR 2.75 trillion of low-cost funding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's 2026 scenario, with the policy rate near 10%, UBL's net interest income from its deposit base is about PKR 380-390bn, which the analyst calls the core earnings engine.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario puts UBL's non-markup income at about PKR 62-67bn, driven by fees and commissions that move with digital banking expansion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank fee and commission income comes from card and ATM charges, remittance and trade finance fees, locker charges and branch-related services, and tends to be stable and gradually growing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario puts UBL's total revenue at about PKR 450-460bn, assuming provisions of PKR 15-17bn that reflect moderate credit costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites UBL's return on equity at around 30% and a deposit base about half in current accounts as the profile that supports a high-profitability view.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL has raised its dividend payout ratio aggressively over two years, including increases quarter on quarter; the analyst's scenario for 2026 is a dividend in the 30-35 range if the current policy holds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says UBL became Pakistan's most profitable bank in 2025 and that this looks like a structural shift from a deposit franchise, not a temporary spike.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL locked roughly PKR 4 trillion of fixed and floating investments at yields of 19-21% starting in Q1 2024, as stated in its September 2024 corporate briefing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Funding the same amount through short-term SBP borrowing, costing about 21% at first and averaging 15-16% in 2024, left a spread of about 5%, or roughly PKR 200bn of one-time gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 2024 windfall only reaches that scale if policy rates fall at the pace seen and inflation declines sharply; a slower fall in rates or inflation would have prevented most of the gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst calls the 2024 locking of high yields a bold but calculated bet that the economy would stabilise and inflation would fall gradually, and says results so far largely validate it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower policy rates stimulate business activity and system liquidity, which grows bank deposits and expands bank balance sheets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks that locked long-term fixed-rate instruments during a high-rate cycle keep earning relatively high returns for several years after rates fall.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In low-rate environments the current account share tends to rise, because customers stop comparing deposit returns closely and keep money in non-interest accounts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lower interest rates tend to support higher price-earnings multiples for listed companies, so bank share prices can rise even if bank profits normalise lower.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst says the PSX showed a V-shaped recovery after the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict and expects similar recovery after geopolitical shocks, while noting history is not a guarantee.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL was founded in 1959 as a private bank, nationalised in 1974, and returned to the private sector through privatisation in 2002.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Best Way Group acquired a controlling stake in UBL during the 2002 privatisation; its founder runs a large retail and wholesale chain in the UK and has made investments in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sees the controlling shareholder's international footprint and governance discipline as adding credibility and investor trust to UBL.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: UBL runs a town hall initiative that brings regional top bankers together for feedback on operating efficiency, and it hires experienced branch managers who bring large corporate and high-net-worth deposit books.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An interest rate swap lets a borrower convert floating-rate loans into fixed-rate ones; the analyst cites a roughly PKR 75bn swap done by UBL as a sign of advanced treasury capability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why UBL Profits Are Rising Banking Business Explained.' (YouTube transcript, undated)
